page: The Vultr voc-m-4c-32gb-800s-amd is an instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It is configured with 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical AMD EPYC cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by 32.0 GB of system memory, which yields a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via an 800 GB NVMe SSD. There are no GPUs bundled with this configuration.

Benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranking in the top tier. However, multi-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores falling in the average range. Memory performance is a notable strength, as evidenced by a PassMark memory score in the top 25% and strong large-block memory write bandwidth. Conversely, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and database operations are weaker, placing in the bottom 25%.

The shared CPU allocation presents a performance tradeoff for sustained multi-threaded workloads, as reflected in the lower multi-threaded decompression and database benchmark tiers. The instance is suited for memory-intensive workloads that do not require continuous, dedicated multi-core compute, such as caching layers, in-memory data structures, and moderate web serving.
